consumer_reviews.snippet:
[L1] **Mode transfer and number law.** $Ue_{m}=\varphi^{\otimes m}$ are orthonormal unit vectors with $NUe_{m}=m\,Ue_{m}$, the count law of a preparation of $Ue_{m}$ is $\delta_{m}$, the count law of the mode-coherent preparation is $e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$, and $\|\psi_{z}\|=1$ ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] clauses (a),(b), [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] clause (b)).

[L2] **Single-mode weights.** For the one-mode Fock space with orthonormal family $(e_{n})$, the weights $w_{n}:=e^{-\beta\omega n}$ satisfy $\sum_{n}w_{n}=(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-1}$ and $\sum_{n}n\,w_{n}=e^{-\beta\omega}(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-2}$, and $\rho_{\beta}=G_{\beta}/Z(\beta)$ is a density operator whose number expectation is $(e^{\beta\omega}-1)^{-1}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] clauses (b),(c),(d)).
consumer_reviews.affected_use: Uses clauses (a),(b) for sharp and Poisson counts, and clause (e) for the full Gibbs limitation.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
4.1 [Why the comparison does not discriminate and what would] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 show equality of the two declared normalised two-bin laws for every datum, so this comparison does not distinguish the two models; agreement with the shared law alone does not establish either model. The models differ in their objects and in their assignments elsewhere: the classical model carries a deterministic intensity and no count law, whereas the quantised model assigns the sharp count law of a number state and the Poisson law of a coherent state under the declared number detector ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b)). An observation could also bear on a comparison with another specified model, provided its detector response, preparation and sampling model are declared in the sense of [F5]. No such comparison is constructed here and no data are reported. This proves (c) and (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F5] ∎

consumer_reviews.snippet:
